nodes.label: handleErrors
nodes.rationale: Scoped error handling: catches anything thrown inside its child (handlers and inner middleware) and sees the original error before any default mapping. Returning null declines and escalates to an outer handler. Nests outside-in like withMiddleware, so the innermost gets first refusal.

nodes.label: fallback
nodes.rationale: Answers any request that matched no route, any method. Because it is wired to each backend's not-found hook it must sit at the root of the route tree - a fallback under path() throws at compile time - and there is at most one per server.

nodes.label: withErrorHandler
nodes.rationale: The server-wide last resort for errors escaping every handleErrors, plus backend-internal errors such as body-parse failures. The place to log your own request id, since the framework's own log line always reads the default header name.

nodes.label: HttpError
nodes.rationale: Maps by default to its status plus an {error, ...extra} JSON body, and can carry response headers such as WWW-Authenticate. A thrown HttpError is not logged at error level - it is a response the handler chose, so it stays on the per-request debug line rather than crying wolf.

nodes.label: Generic 500 redaction
nodes.rationale: The default 500 carries only {error: 'Internal Server Error'} because thrown text routinely holds file paths, SQL fragments, connection strings or a stack, and a 500 is by definition a case nobody wrote a message for. The redaction only works because the detail survives server-side: every escaping throw is logged at error with the error value passed through.

nodes.label: Error-handling precedence
nodes.rationale: Three ordered layers: innermost-to-outermost handleErrors (original thrown value, may decline with null), then withErrorHandler (escapees plus backend-internal errors), then the framework default. A handler that throws at step 1 or 2 hands the new error to the next layer.
